title: Franco Ferrara Giovinezza.wmv
description:
Arturo Ferrara

1900 (1903?) Francavilla di Sicilia -- 1983 Giardini-Naxos


Ferrara studied singing in Milan. Ferrara made his debut at the Teatra Alambra in Taranto as Cavaradossi at age twenty three ( Kutsch & Riemens states that he studied with Maestro Franco Marucci and made his debut in 1924 at the Teatro Alhambra in Bari as Cavaradossi).
During the next fifteen years, he had great successes in the Italian and foreign Opera Houses, including Japan, China, Jugoslavia, and Egypt.

His career evolved as follows according to the Italian musical newspapers:

1925 Cairo, Alessandria d'Egitto
1926 Alessandria d'Egitto, Cairo, Porto Said
1927 Catanzano
1930 Piacenza
1931 Roma, Torino
1932 Palermo, Cagliari, Napoli, Roma, Torino
1933 Malta, Napoli, Venezia, Roma, Torino
1934 Genova, Cagliari, Roma, Torino, Trieste
1935 Salerno, Roma, Torino
1938 Adria
1939 Modena, Parma (Regio)
1950 Messina
He retired at the beginning of the war and went back to Francavilla.
His repertory included (Ferrara told his colleagues that his repertory consisted of 89 operas with many unusual ones): Rodolfo, Herodes. Des Grieux (Manon Lescaut), Dafni (Dafni by Mulè), Ippolito (Fedra), Giovanni (Giovanni Gallurese), Azaele (Il figliuol profigo), Rinuccio, Edgardo, Ludovico (La Baronessa di Carini by Mulè), Vitaliano (Romanticismo by Robbiani), Florindo (I dispettosi amanti by Parelli), Edoardo (Il grillo del focolare by Zandonai), Fazio (La leggenda delle sette torri by Gasco), Osaka, Enzo, Federico (Germania), La Wally, Pedru (La monacella della fontana by Mulè), Tedesco (Bacco in Toscana by Castelnuovo Tedesco), Baldo (Belfago by Respighi), Pery, Bruno (Il mistero by Monleone), Turiddu, Alfredo, Folco (Fanfulla by Parelli), Sir Oluf (Sir Oluf by Malatesta), Cavaliere (Il Miraculo by Laccetti), Duca, ? (Al Lupo by Mulè), ..


In the 2007, the municipality of Francavilla named the refurbished Cinema Comunale Arturo Ferrara.
